items.title: NSE overhauls closing price discovery, changes F&O expiry settlement rules from December 7
items.description: The NSE has announced changes to the Closing Auction Session (CAS) in the equity cash segment and trading rules in the equity derivatives segment, effective December 7, 2026. In two circulars issued on November 6.

items.title: Concurrent Gainers: 9 stocks gain for 5 days in a row
items.description: Over the five trading sessions ending November 6, the Sensex surged 8.82%, or 6,568 points, to close at 81,028, marking gains in each of the five sessions. Amid this broad-based rally, around 45 stocks from the BSE 200 index advanced in all five consecutive sessions from November 2 to 6. Of these, we shortlisted 9 stocks that consistently gained throughout the period, delivering cumulative returns ranging from 15% to 20%. (Data Source: ACE Equity)

items.title: Muhurat Trading 2026: How to trade during the special session tomorrow to welcome Samvat 2083?
items.description: Indian stock exchanges BSE and NSE will conduct the special one-hour Muhurat Trading session on Sunday from 2:20 pm to 3:30 pm to mark the beginning of Samvat 2083. The session, a long-standing Diwali tradition coinciding with Lakshmi Puja, typically sees lower trading volumes. Analysts have advised investors to remain selective with their bets during the auspicious session.

items.title: Stocks vs Gold: Which asset could create more wealth in the Samvat 2083?
items.description: Samco Securities believes Indian equities are attractively valued against gold, with the Sensex-to-Gold ratio near multi-decade lows. It recommends increasing equity exposure in Samvat 2083 while retaining gold as a hedge, diversifying across sectors and geographies, and considering US ETFs amid crude oil, currency and global market risks.

items.title: D-Street just 5% away from highs with a 10% bounce from lows
items.description: The rupee has shown a significant recovery, closing at 93.90 this week, its best level since April. Recent drops in oil prices have alleviated inflation concerns and supported the local currency. Simultaneously, foreign portfolio investors have made substantial net purchases in Indian equities, contributing to market stability. Indian equity indices have also rallied over 10% from recent lows, showing strong earnings.

items.title: D Street lights up, ends Diwali week with a firecracker of a Friday
items.description: Indian stocks witnessed impressive growth, with the Sensex and Nifty surging over 2%, defying declines in Asian markets. This robust rally is fueled by strong corporate earnings coupled with declining crude oil prices, boosting investor morale significantly. Over the recent weeks, foreign portfolio investors have surpassed net purchases of $4 billion, enhancing the positive outlook.

items.title: Dalal Street Week Ahead: Nifty bulls come back to life, but 25,000–25,200 zone poses next test
items.description: Indian equity markets rallied significantly following the results of the US midterm elections, which were favorable for investors. The Nifty Index saw a large gain and reclaimed important moving averages, indicating improved market sentiment. Some consolidation is expected, as the Index approaches broader resistance levels between 25,000 and 25,200. Various sector indices showed differing momentum as they contrasted against the broader Nifty 500 Index.

items.title: FIIs pump Rs 45,960 crore into Indian stocks in a week; is the tide finally turning for Dalal Street?
items.description: Foreign institutional investors poured a net Rs 45,960 crore into Indian equities in one week, reversing October’s outflows and fuelling a sharp market rally. Improving earnings, attractive valuations and global AI stock corrections are driving renewed interest. However, sustainability of inflows, crude prices and geopolitical risks remain key concerns.
